prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: After the full first round I keep B017 as my preferred configuration. It is the one shortlisted achievement where a specific, non-obvious prediction (the 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, with flat bands at a magic angle) was followed by an experiment (2018) that showed correlated insulators and superconductivity and then opened a new regime of physics. The existence of the phases is not in doubt: many independent groups reproduce them, and the platform has spread to other moire systems. The chair's maturity question is answered, for me, by the citation rather than by delay: a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated and superconducting states makes no claim about the pairing mechanism, so the open mechanism does not touch what is being honoured. The theory-plus-experiment structure fits the three-name limit without forcing out anyone who is clearly necessary.
statement.case_against: My reservations from round 1 remain and I have not fully dissolved them. The discovery dates from 2018, the mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved, and Yuan Cao as first author, the Dean, Young, Kim and Yazdani groups, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto sit outside the credited names; a citation cannot repair that. B015 is the stronger candidate on maturity and cleanliness of credit, and the committee could reasonably prefer it this year on those grounds. I weigh it second because its principal payoffs (a redefined second, geodesy, dark-matter searches) are still partly prospective and because it extends a recognised line from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, but that is a judgement about breadth, not about quality. I dropped B012 from my alternatives for this round because of my proximity to it and the 2025 prize.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, prefers B015 on the grounds of a clean figure of merit, reproduction in Sr, Yb and Hg clocks and a clean two-name credit, and asks whether the 2005 and 2012 prizes make it incremental.
responses.response: I accept his and Kroll-Stefan's argument that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct principle (many-atom parallelism with the light shift cancelled) and not a repeat of comb or ion-clock work, so I do not use overlap as an argument against B015. That is why it stays my first alternative and why I would not call it an error if the committee chose it. Where I still differ is weight: I do not think that waiting for the redefinition of the second strengthens B015, and I think the opening of a new regime of matter outweighs a further decade of precision.

responses.point: Danielsson treats the unresolved pairing mechanism as irrelevant to a discovery prize and wants the citation to name the prediction and the discovery of the states.
responses.response: On the question of principle I now agree more than I did in round 1. Existence and reproducibility, not mechanism, are the test for a discovery prize, and my earlier unease belongs to the wording and not to a decision to defer. I would keep the citation to the flat-band prediction and the observation of the correlated and superconducting states, and avoid the words twistronics or any explanation of pairing, so that the omissions of Cao and the other groups are easier to defend.

responses.point: Eriksson would credit only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero for B017, and prefers B051 first as the most mature candidate with a two-decade record.
responses.response: I considered the two-name version seriously, since it would also leave one place free. I keep Bistritzer because the 2011 prediction is one joint paper with MacDonald, and crediting MacDonald alone would assign to one author a result that belongs to two. I accept his point that B051 is the most mature of the three leading candidates and is why I list it among my alternatives. I still cannot resolve the Mele or Hasan seat and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang boundary within three names, which is why it is not my preference.

responses.point: Kroll answers the chair's question by saying that the case for B015 is weaker if the committee wants a prize for a new phase of matter, and lists B016 as an alternative.
responses.response: That is the criterion I am applying, and under it B017 ranks ahead of B015 for me; I would answer the chair's second question yes. I do not move B016 into my alternatives, because five names for three places forces an arbitrary cut, and, as someone in quantum-technology work through WACQT, I would discount my own judgement in that area.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B015 first but treats B017 as likely timing-limited and describes the omission of Yuan Cao as a difficulty the citation cannot repair.
responses.response: I agree about Cao and have no tidy remedy within the three-name cap. I do not think the timing objection improves with delay, since the mechanism question may stay open for many years and the attribution does not get easier. If the committee decides the omission of Cao is decisive, the honest alternative is B015 and not a different B017 trio.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts a citation limited to prediction and observation of the phases as sufficient answer to the maturity objection.
Whether Bistritzer should be named alongside MacDonald, or whether a two-name B017 would be the more defensible compact configuration.
How much weight the committee should give to the omission of Yuan Cao and the other experimental groups, which the three-name cap does not allow us to fix.
Whether the pending redefinition of the second makes B015 the safer choice this year, and whether I am discounting its prospective payoffs too much.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: I work on circuit QED theory, I am a Chalmers colleague of Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson, I direct WACQT, and I share an institution with Olsson-Eva. For that reason I do not prefer B012 and have removed it from my alternatives; I would recuse myself if it were put to a vote. I see no specific conflict for B017, B015 or B051, and I have no documented tie to MacDonald, Bistritzer, Jarillo-Herrero, Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp.
